- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true +15%), apply mean reversion bias: subtract 5–8% from next 3 periods to prevent overhang.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.25–0.5) and forecast diverges from history mean, align forecast toward 3-period moving average of past 18 days.  
- For horizon > 14 days, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment spikes — sentiment should only adjust forecast if >0.85 confidence.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), check for sentiment lag — if sentiment is positive but forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days.
